jordana: FYI onboarding Llama->Qwen conversion hit a weird tokenization+rotary wrap problem after int8 fast quant. Symptoms: occasional early-termination and duplicated backticks in code outputs, and a small but reproducible BLEU drop on our codegen eval. Anyone seen a tokenizer offset + rotary index wrap interact like this? :confused:
matt: can you share the conversion command, quant flags, and a tiny failing example? also which tokenizer (sentencepiece/byte-level) were you using during convert?
jordana: commands below. using spm for Llama vocab, converting to qwen layout map via `--map-policy permute-heads` because Qwen uses different head ordering. quant backend: our-kernel/int8-fast.
```
lm-convert --src llama-13b.safetensors --tgt qwen-13b.safetensors --map-policy permute-heads --vocab-map src2qwen.json
qtool quant --model qwen-13b.safetensors --dtype int8 --mode fast --backend our-kernel
```

pavel: quick thoughts: permuting head order + packing quant can accidentally shift rotary index if converter assumes fixed head_dim layout. Also SPM->byte merges may collapse ZWJ/soft-hyphen into same token id which shifts offsets in longer sequences. Do you have a minimal failing prompt and output?
jordana: minimal prompt attached inline (trimmed):
"""
Prompt: ```python
# compute factorial
def fact(n):
    if n == 0:
        return 1
    # compute recursively
    return n * fact(n-1)
```
Expected: pretty-printed function.
Got (int8 fast): truncated at "```" then repeated triple backticks and a second code fence that starts but has garbage tokens.
"""

ml-bot: automated eval summary for this conversion run:
- float32 baseline: BLEU_code=42.1, code-acc=88.6
- int8(fast): BLEU_code=38.3, code-acc=84.0
- int8(slow): BLEU_code=40.8, code-acc=86.2
- sample-flaky-rate: 1.4% (truncated or duplicate fences)
(ticket: #t-2026-41)

liz: interesting that slow/int8 reduces but doesn't eliminate the issue. suggests quantization amplifies a structural mismatch (tokenization offsets or rotary index). two quick tries: 1) run quant with `--preserve-vocab-ids` so we don't remap soft/hyphen/ZWJ tokens, 2) run converter with `--explicit-headmap` instead of `permute-heads` to avoid implicit reorder assumptions.
omar: also add a sanity check in the runtime: assert that kv_cache indexing plus rotary index mod head_dim == expected for the first N tokens. we had a similar assert when onboarding Mistral a while ago. I can push a tiny assert patch to runtime.
matt: can you dump the converted model's `rotary_freq` and `head_dim` arrays? if head_dim mismatches packaging assumptions then the kernel might read wrong strides.
jordana: dumped snippets:
```
MODEL-CONV: head_dim=128, head_count=80
ROTARY: src_rotary_freq_len=160, tgt_rotary_freq_len=160
HEADER: head_order=permuted by map src->(3,1,0,2,...)
CONV_NOTE: applied group_norm_fold=true
```

pavel: group_norm_fold=true is suspicious. group folding sometimes multiplies per-head rotary scales into a group weight. combined with permuted head ordering this can produce inconsistent per-head phases. propose: re-run convert with `--disable-fold-norm` and `--explicit-headmap` and then quantize with `--calibrate-per-head` mode. Also run tokenization diff to ensure SPM merges didn't collapse critical tokens: `token-diff --src-vocab llama.sp.model --tgt-vocab qwen.sp.model --check-zwj --check-soft-hyphen`.
liz: adding to that: run a tiny eval where you keep all float rotary params but quantize everything else (float rotary preserved). command: `qtool quant --preserve-rotary --model qwen-13b.safetensors --dtype int8 --mode fast` and compare. if preserving rotary fixes it, conversion is the culprit.
jordana: will try all three. timeline: quick experiments now, longer 10k evals later tonight. i also added the minimal repro to the ticket.
omar: i pushed the runtime assert to branch `asserts/kv-rotary-check-9098` and it will log when kv index vs rotary index diverge. if you can run a dev build it will surface where the wrap happens.
matt: small note: when head permutation is odd, the KV cache layout (NHWC vs NCHW style packing) can be read with wrong stride if the runtime assumes original order; that shows up only after packing/quant because packed layout uses contiguous blocks. worth double-checking the packer.
ml-bot: triage update: labels `tokenizer-edgecase`, `rotary-wrap`, `quant-variance`. assigned to @jordana and @pavel. priority-medium.
jordana: quick results: disabling norm fold + explicit headmap + preserve-rotary during quant yields BLEU_code=41.9, code-acc=88.2, sample-flaky-rate=0.2% on 1k sample. preserving rotary alone gave BLEU=40.6. looks like a combination of group-fold + permute + fast quant packing caused index misread. full 10k run queued (job 5123).
pavel: thanks for the data. action items: (1) add conversion lint that errors when `group_norm_fold` is enabled together with `map-policy permute-heads`, (2) add token-diff check to convert CI to detect ZWJ/soft-hyphen merges, (3) add runtime assert for kv/rotary index alignment. i'll file follow-up PRs.
liz: i'll own a shortplay doc with conversion best-practices for cross-arch headmaps and quant knobs.
jordana: closing loop here. will update ticket with final 10k numbers later. thanks all. :raised_hands:
